text:
GSDP contribution in National GDP
Note – Mr. Chandrababu Naidu in this press meet and also in his entire trip to Davos, made baseless allegations that the State of Andhra Pradesh had undergone a period of severe economic hardship and financial mismanagement owing to the polices of the State Government during the period 2019-24. 
It is a tragedy that, despite an improvement of the State Government’s performance on several fronts between 2019-24, Mr. Naidu chose to make baseless allegations purely for political ends.
Does this improvement in State’s contribution to National GDP during 2019-24 indicate economic distress to Mr. Naidu?

text:
Capital Expenditure
The capital expenditure incurred during the first six months of this financial year is only Rs. 4,613.61 crores. The budget documents estimate the capital expenditure for the entire year at Rs. 32,712.84 crores. Which means, for the second six months of this financial year an amount of Rs. 28,099.23 crores of capital expenditure has to be incurred. Is this possible? Further, the budget documents suggest that, the amount estimated to be received as Central Assistance for Capital Expenditure is Rs. 12,950 crores. The amount budget by Central Government for all States is Rs. 1,50,000 crores. In this case, can we expect to receive such high share?

text:
Actual picture regarding sectoral capital expenditure
Note - Mr. Naidu has presented that with respect to social services, the capital expenditure in 2022-23 was lower than that during 2018-19 and with this isolated comparison between only two years, is trying to say that the capital expenditure in the crucial social sector that encompasses education, health, water supply, sanitation and urban development, social welfare and nutrition, has reduced by 84.3%. In fact, he blatantly lied that since 2018-19, the capital expenditure on social services sector has reduced. This is completely false.

As can be seen in the table, the average capital incurred in social services sector during 2019-24 is more than double of what was incurred during 2014-19.

text:
Debt sustainability (Central Govt. Vs AP Govt. 2014-19)
Mr. Naidu has specified a definition that indicates debt sustainability. The definition in is as follow - 
Growth Rate of Interest Payments  >  GSDP Growth Rate.


Going by this definition, during 2014-19, Central Government was in the zone of debt sustainability whereas, AP Government was in a zone of ‘zero’ debt sustainability.
* The interest payments by the State Government during 2013-14 were to the tune of Rs. 12,911 crores and of this 58% pertains to the successor State of AP.
Source - CAG and MOSPI

text:
Comparison between growth of tax revenues and GSDP
Note - The principal behind proportionate growth in tax revenues and GDSP is that, higher consumption and investment inevitably results in higher revenues for the Government on account of taxes such as GST, sales tax, excise and on account of charges under the head stamps and registration and so forth. With a year-on-year revenue growth to date of 1.10%, it is impossible for the GSDP to grow at 12.94% in this year.

text:
Actual picture conveying the Revenue growth
Note - Mr. Naidu’s presentation demonstrates his intention to mislead the public into believing that the State’s own tax revenues grew during this period at a year-on-year rate of 17.10%. However, the CAGR of State’s own tax revenues during the period of TDP Government between 2014-19 was 12.9% and the same during the period of the YSRCP Government was to the tune of 10.0%. This is despite the occurrence of unprecedented global economic distress in the face of the pandemic outbreak during the period of the YSRCP Government.
